model_name: Repressilator: symmetric cyclic transcriptional negative-feedback oscillator (Elowitz & Leibler 2000, Box 1, deterministic continuous model)
description: A synthetic network in E. coli in which three transcriptional repressors (LacI, TetR and lambda CI) repress one another in a cycle: LacI represses tetR, TetR represses cI, and CI represses lacI. Box 1 of the paper gives six coupled first-order ODEs for the three mRNA concentrations (m_i) and the three protein concentrations (p_i). Each mRNA is transcribed from a promoter repressed by the previous repressor via a Hill function with coefficient n and leakiness alpha0, and is degraded with rate 1 (time is rescaled in units of the mRNA lifetime). Each protein is translated from its mRNA (rate beta, which is also the protein-to-mRNA decay ratio) and decays with rate beta. The model predicts either convergence to a stable steady state or sustained limit-cycle oscillations depending on (alpha, beta, n, alpha0).

variables.name: m_lacI
variables.description: Concentration of lacI mRNA, rescaled by the translation efficiency (average proteins produced per mRNA)

variables.name: m_tetR
variables.description: Concentration of tetR mRNA, rescaled by the translation efficiency

variables.name: m_cI
variables.description: Concentration of lambda cI mRNA, rescaled by the translation efficiency

variables.name: p_lacI
variables.description: LacI protein concentration, in units of K_M

variables.name: p_tetR
variables.description: TetR protein concentration, in units of K_M

variables.name: p_cI
variables.description: lambda CI protein concentration, in units of K_M

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Effective maximum transcription+translation rate (promoter strength times translation efficiency, dimensionlessly rescaled). Derived from the paper's stated dimensional values: max promoter strength 0.5 transcripts/s, translation rate 0.167 proteins per mRNA per s (=20 proteins per transcript / 120 s), K_M=40 monomers/cell, mRNA half-life 2 min, protein half-life 10 min -> alpha = k_r*k_t/(beta*K_M*lambda_m^2) = 0.5*0.1667/(0.2*40*(ln2/120)^2) = 313.

parameters.name: alpha0
parameters.description: Leakiness of the promoter: residual protein production in the presence of saturating repressor. Paper gives repressed promoter strength 5e-4 transcripts/s vs 0.5 fully induced, i.e. alpha0/alpha = 1e-3.

parameters.name: beta
parameters.description: Ratio of protein decay rate to mRNA decay rate (Box 1: 'b denotes the ratio of the protein decay rate to the mRNA decay rate'). From protein half-life 10 min and mRNA half-life 2 min: beta = (ln2/10)/(ln2/2) = 0.2.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Hill coefficient describing cooperativity of transcriptional repression (Box 1: 'Hill coefficient, n = 2').

origin.source_text: Elowitz, M. B. & Leibler, S. 'A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators', Nature 403, 335-338 (2000), Box 1 (deterministic continuous approximation).
assumptions: Symmetric repressilator: the three repressor modules are treated as identical except for DNA-binding specificity, so a single set of parameters applies to all six ODEs.

Deterministic, continuous approximation: molecular species are treated as continuous concentrations, neglecting the discrete and stochastic nature of reactions (the paper also gives a stochastic version).
Transcription rate depends on the repressor concentration through a Hill function with coefficient n; the promoter has a constant leak alpha0.
Time is rescaled in units of the mRNA lifetime; protein concentrations are in units of K_M; mRNA concentrations are rescaled by translation efficiency.
Protein translation rate equals beta times mRNA level, and protein decay rate also equals beta (in these units).

missing_information: Explicit initial conditions (m_i and p_i at t=0) used for the numerical integration in Fig. 1c are not reported in the paper, so the ODE system as written has no fully specified initial state.

The dimensionless value of alpha used for Fig. 1c is not printed directly; it had to be derived from the stated dimensional rates (0.5 transcripts/s, 0.167 proteins mRNA^-1 s^-1, K_M=40, mRNA half-life 2 min, protein half-life 10 min), which introduces some uncertainty.
The precise functional form of the transcription term for the generalized/non-symmetric case, and the exact rescaled units of the plotted axes in Fig. 1b, are hard to read from the OCR text.
No explicit time units/axes for the model output in Fig. 1c beyond 'Time (min)' up to ~600 min.
